summary.text: One of the nine sons of Priam whom the old king summoned when he set out to ransom Hector — a namesake of Antiphus son of Hecuba in Apollodorus' stemma and of allied captains elsewhere in the poem.

story.text: Priam chid Antiphonus among the nine sons he called to harness the wagon for sacred Ilios: Helenus and Paris, goodly Agathon, Pammon, Polites good at the war-cry, Deïphobus, Hippothous, and lordly Dius — base children who had not died for Hector.
